words.defn_en: an excuse:

sentences.en: He used a doctor's appointment as a ______ to leave the meeting early.
sentences.zh: 他以看醫生為藉口提早離開會議。

sentences.en: The soldiers invaded the town under the ______ of restoring order.
sentences.zh: 士兵們以恢復秩序為藉口入侵了這座城鎮。

words.defn_en: reaching maturity early:

sentences.en: The ______ child could already read novels by the age of five.
sentences.zh: 這個早熟的孩子五歲就已經能閱讀小說了。

sentences.en: Her ______ talent for music amazed everyone at the recital.
sentences.zh: 她在音樂方面早熟的天賦讓演奏會上的每個人都驚豔不已。

words.defn_en: forewarning:

sentences.en: She had a strange ______ that something bad was about to happen.
sentences.zh: 她有一種奇怪的預感,覺得將有不好的事情發生。

sentences.en: His ______ about the storm turned out to be correct.
sentences.zh: 他對這場暴風雨的預感後來證實是正確的。

words.defn_en: proposition for argument:

sentences.en: The whole argument rests on the ______ that everyone acts in their own self-interest.
sentences.zh: 整個論點都建立在人人都出於自身利益行事這個前提上。

sentences.en: If the initial ______ is false, the entire conclusion falls apart.
sentences.zh: 如果最初的假設是錯誤的,整個結論就會站不住腳。

words.defn_en: to hasten, cause:

sentences.en: The assassination helped to ______ the outbreak of war.
sentences.zh: 這起暗殺事件促成了戰爭的爆發。

sentences.en: A sudden drop in temperature can ______ the formation of ice crystals.
sentences.zh: 氣溫驟降能促成冰晶的形成。

words.defn_en: to prevent:

sentences.en: A prior commitment will ______ him from attending the wedding.
sentences.zh: 先前的行程安排使他無法參加這場婚禮。

sentences.en: New safety regulations are designed to ______ future accidents.
sentences.zh: 新的安全法規旨在防止未來發生意外。

words.defn_en: introduction:

sentences.en: The small protest turned out to be just a ______ to a much larger uprising.
sentences.zh: 這場小規模的抗議結果只是一場更大規模起義的序幕。

sentences.en: The composer's early works served as a ______ to his later masterpieces.
sentences.zh: 這位作曲家早期的作品成為他後來傑作的前奏。

words.defn_en: primary, common, general:

sentences.en: Obesity has become increasingly ______ in modern society.
sentences.zh: 肥胖問題在現代社會中變得越來越普遍。

sentences.en: The disease is most ______ in regions with poor sanitation.
sentences.zh: 這種疾病在衛生條件不佳的地區最為盛行。

words.defn_en: earlier example of something similar:

sentences.en: The court's ruling set an important legal ______.
sentences.zh: 這項法院判決樹立了一個重要的法律先例。

sentences.en: Allowing one exception could set a dangerous ______ for the future.
sentences.zh: 允許一次例外可能會為未來立下危險的先例。

words.defn_en: exclusive power or right:

sentences.en: It is the president's ______ to appoint new cabinet members.
sentences.zh: 任命新的內閣成員是總統的特權。

sentences.en: Choosing her own career path was a ______ she valued deeply.
sentences.zh: 選擇自己的職業道路是她非常珍視的一項特權。

words.defn_en: lie, deviation from the truth:

sentences.en: The witness's ______ frustrated the lawyers on both sides.
sentences.zh: 這位證人閃爍其詞的說法讓雙方律師都感到十分沮喪。

sentences.en: His constant ______ made it hard to trust anything he said.
sentences.zh: 他不斷含糊其辭,讓人很難相信他所說的任何話。

words.defn_en: too forward or bold; overstepping proper bounds

sentences.en: It would be ______ of me to assume I already have the job.
sentences.zh: 假設自己已經得到這份工作,那未免太自以為是了。

sentences.en: She found his ______ request for a raise, made on his first day, quite bold.
sentences.zh: 她覺得他上班第一天就冒昧地要求加薪,實在太大膽了。

words.defn_en: claiming or pretending increased importance or grandness

sentences.en: The restaurant's ______ menu described a simple salad in absurdly fancy terms.
sentences.zh: 這家餐廳自命不凡的菜單用荒謬華麗的詞彙來描述一道簡單的沙拉。

sentences.en: His ______ use of big words didn't impress anyone at the meeting.
sentences.zh: 他在會議上刻意賣弄艱深詞彙,自命不凡的樣子並沒有讓任何人印象深刻。

words.defn_en: one who takes advantage of another, exploits or feeds on another; a strong adversary or rival

sentences.en: The lion is a top ______ in the African savanna.
sentences.zh: 獅子是非洲大草原上的頂級掠食者。

sentences.en: Online scammers act as ______s, targeting the elderly and vulnerable.
sentences.zh: 網路詐騙者如同掠食者一般,專門鎖定老年人和弱勢族群下手。

words.defn_en: novel; unparalleled

sentences.en: The pandemic caused ______ disruptions to the global economy.
sentences.zh: 這場疫情對全球經濟造成了前所未有的衝擊。

sentences.en: Ticket sales reached ______ levels for the reunion concert.
sentences.zh: 這場重聚演唱會的票券銷售達到了空前的水準。

words.defn_en: an understanding or perception formed in advance:
words.root_note: prae- (before) + apprehendere (to seize, understand), from Latin

sentences.en: Her ______ of the difficult negotiation proved largely accurate.
sentences.zh: 她對這場困難談判的預先認知結果證明大致準確。

sentences.en: Philosophers debated whether all knowledge begins with some form of ______ .
sentences.zh: 哲學家爭論所有知識是否都始於某種形式的先入之見。

words.defn_en: the face of a cliff, a steep or overhanging place:

sentences.en: The hikers stopped just short of the ______, their hearts pounding.
sentences.zh: 這群健行者在懸崖邊緣停下腳步,心跳劇烈。

sentences.en: The country stood on the ______ of economic collapse.
sentences.zh: 這個國家正站在經濟崩潰的懸崖邊緣。

words.defn_en: supposed knowledge of an event before it happens:
words.root_note: prae- (before) + cognitio (knowledge), from Latin cognoscere (to know)

sentences.en: She claimed to have had a moment of ______ before the accident occurred.
sentences.zh: 她聲稱在這起意外發生前有過一瞬間的預知感。

sentences.en: Scientists remain skeptical of claims involving ______ .
sentences.zh: 科學家對涉及預知能力的主張始終抱持懷疑態度。

words.defn_en: a person or thing that precedes and leads to the development of something else:

sentences.en: The telegraph served as a ______ to modern telecommunications.
sentences.zh: 電報作為現代電信通訊的先驅。

sentences.en: Historians consider the pamphlet a ______ to the revolutionary movement.
sentences.zh: 歷史學家認為這本小冊子是這場革命運動的先驅。

words.defn_en: to decide or determine in advance, especially by fate or a higher power:

sentences.en: His actions seemed ______, as if everything had already been decided for him.
sentences.zh: 他的行動看起來像是命中註定,彷彿一切早已被預先決定好了。

sentences.en: The results of the rigged election were entirely ______.
sentences.zh: 這場舞弊選舉的結果完全是預先決定好的。

words.defn_en: decided in advance:

sentences.en: The outcome seemed ______ and that we could do nothing to change it.
sentences.zh: 這個結果似乎是預先決定的,我們無法做任何改變。

sentences.en: Each contestant was given a ______ amount of time to answer.
sentences.zh: 每位參賽者都被分配到一段預先決定好的答題時間。

words.defn_en: to say what will happen in the future:

sentences.en: Meteorologists ______ rain tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 氣象學家預測明天會下雨。

sentences.en: No one could ______ how successful the small startup would become.
sentences.zh: 沒有人能預測這家小型新創公司會變得如此成功。

words.defn_en: a preference or inclination for something:

sentences.en: She has always had a ______ for mystery novels over any other genre.
sentences.zh: 比起其他任何類型,她一直對懸疑小說情有獨鍾。

sentences.en: His ______ for spicy food often surprised his dinner guests.
sentences.zh: 他對辛辣食物的偏好常常讓晚宴賓客感到意外。

words.defn_en: to make someone susceptible to a particular condition or behavior beforehand:

sentences.en: Genetics can ______ certain individuals to particular illnesses.
sentences.zh: 基因可能使某些人容易罹患特定的疾病。

sentences.en: Early childhood experiences often ______ people toward certain habits.
sentences.zh: 早期的童年經驗往往使人們傾向於形成特定的習慣。

words.defn_en: a tendency to a particular condition or behavior, existing beforehand:

sentences.en: Doctors asked about any family ______ to heart disease.
sentences.zh: 醫生詢問是否有任何心臟病的家族先天傾向。

sentences.en: Her ______ toward anxiety made public speaking especially difficult.
sentences.zh: 她天生容易焦慮的傾向讓公開演講變得格外困難。

words.defn_en: surpassing all others; distinguished above all others:
words.root_note: prae- (before) + eminere (to stand out), from Latin

sentences.en: She is regarded as the ______ expert in her field of study.
sentences.zh: 她被視為她研究領域中首屈一指的專家。

sentences.en: The university attracted the ______ scholars of the century.
sentences.zh: 這所大學吸引了這個世紀最卓越的學者。

words.defn_en: a greater liking for one option over another:

sentences.en: She stated a clear ______ for tea over coffee.
sentences.zh: 她明確表示了對茶而非咖啡的偏好。

sentences.en: The survey asked customers about their ______ s regarding delivery times.
sentences.zh: 這項調查詢問顧客對送貨時間的偏好。

words.defn_en: a preconceived opinion not based on reason; to cause bias:

sentences.en: The community worked hard to overcome longstanding racial ______ .
sentences.zh: 這個社區努力克服長期存在的種族偏見。

sentences.en: The lawyer argued that pretrial publicity could ______ the jury.
sentences.zh: 這位律師主張審判前的媒體報導可能會影響陪審團的公正。

words.defn_en: relating to the innocent period before a significant fall or loss:
words.defn_zh: 墮落之前的;純真時期的
words.root_note: prae- (before) + lapsus (a fall), from Latin labi (to slip)

sentences.en: The novel evokes a ______ innocence before the war destroyed everything.
sentences.zh: 這本小說喚起了戰爭摧毀一切之前那份墮落之前的純真。

sentences.en: She longed for the ______ simplicity of her childhood summers.
sentences.zh: 她渴望回到童年夏日那份未經世事的純真簡單。

words.defn_en: preceding and preparing for something more important:

sentences.en: The doctor ordered a ______ blood test before the full diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 醫生在做出完整診斷前安排了一項初步的血液檢查。

sentences.en: The ______ results looked promising for the new drug trial.
sentences.zh: 這項新藥試驗的初步結果看起來相當有希望。

words.defn_en: planned beforehand:

sentences.en: Because the man had planned the theft for weeks, it was obvious the crime was ______.
sentences.zh: 由於這名男子已經策劃這起竊案好幾個星期,顯然這是一起預謀犯罪。

sentences.en: The prosecutor argued that the attack was clearly ______.
sentences.zh: 檢察官主張這起攻擊事件顯然是有預謀的。

words.defn_en: giving warning of something in advance:

sentences.en: A dull headache served as a ______ sign of the coming migraine.
sentences.zh: 一陣隱隱的頭痛作為即將到來的偏頭痛的預兆徵兆。

sentences.en: She experienced a ______ dream the night before the earthquake.
sentences.zh: 她在這場地震前一晚做了一個帶有預兆意味的夢。

words.defn_en: superiority in importance or quantity:

sentences.en: The jury found a clear ______ of evidence pointing to his guilt.
sentences.zh: 陪審團發現大量證據明顯指向他有罪。

sentences.en: A ______ of young voters supported the new candidate.
sentences.zh: 大多數年輕選民都支持這位新候選人。

words.defn_en: to influence someone beforehand, especially favorably:
words.defn_zh: 使先入為主;使產生好感
words.root_note: prae- (before) + possess, from Latin possidere (to have and hold)

sentences.en: His charming manner tended to ______ new acquaintances in his favor.
sentences.zh: 他迷人的舉止總是讓新結識的人對他先入為主地產生好感。

sentences.en: Her glowing reputation would ______ even the sternest interviewers.
sentences.zh: 她耀眼的名聲總是能讓即使最嚴厲的面試官都先產生好感。

words.defn_en: occupying the mind to the exclusion of other thoughts:
words.defn_zh: 先入為主的/占據心思的

sentences.en: A ______ fear of failure kept him from ever submitting his manuscript.
sentences.zh: 一股先入為主的失敗恐懼,讓他始終不敢遞交自己的手稿。

sentences.en: Her ______ worry about the exam made it hard to focus on anything else.
sentences.zh: 她對這場考試揮之不去的擔憂,讓她難以專注在其他任何事情上。

words.defn_en: an omen:

sentences.en: The old sailors viewed the strange cloud formation as a ______ of the storm.
sentences.zh: 老水手們將這片奇異的雲層視為暴風雨的預兆。

sentences.en: Her sudden illness felt like a grim ______ of what was to come.
sentences.zh: 她突如其來的病痛,彷彿是即將發生之事的不祥預兆。

words.defn_en: knowledge of events before they happen; foresight:

sentences.en: Her uncanny ______ allowed her to anticipate the market crash.
sentences.zh: 她驚人的先見之明讓她能夠預見這場市場崩盤。

sentences.en: The author's ______ about future technology impressed later readers.
sentences.zh: 這位作者對未來科技的先見之明讓後世的讀者印象深刻。

words.defn_en: to have foreknowledge of events:

sentences.en: Her ______ warnings about the market crash proved entirely accurate.
sentences.zh: 她對市場崩盤具有先見之明的警告,後來證實完全正確。

sentences.en: The novel's ______ depiction of future technology impressed critics decades later.
sentences.zh: 這部小說對未來科技具有先見之明的描寫,數十年後仍讓評論家印象深刻。

words.defn_en: to recommend or authorize the use of something, especially a treatment or remedy:

sentences.en: The doctor will ______ a course of antibiotics to treat the infection.
sentences.zh: 醫生將開立一個療程的抗生素來治療這次感染。

sentences.en: The doctor ______ antibiotics when I had an ear infection.
sentences.zh: 我耳朵感染時,醫生開了抗生素給我。

words.defn_en: an instruction written by a doctor for medicine; an authoritative recommendation:

sentences.en: She picked up her ______ from the pharmacy after work.
sentences.zh: 她下班後到藥局取了她的處方藥。

sentences.en: The economist offered a bold ______ for reviving the economy.
sentences.zh: 這位經濟學家提出了一項大膽的振興經濟處方。

words.defn_en: an intuitive feeling about the future, especially of something bad:
words.root_note: prae- (before) + sentire (to feel), from Latin, via French

sentences.en: She had a strange ______ that something was wrong before the phone rang.
sentences.zh: 電話鈴響之前,她有一種奇怪的預感,覺得事情不太對勁。

sentences.en: A dark ______ settled over the household on the eve of the storm.
sentences.zh: 在暴風雨來臨的前夕,一種不祥的預感籠罩了這個家庭。

words.defn_en: to keep something in its original state:

sentences.en: The builders worked to ______ the house's original decorations.
sentences.zh: 建築工人努力保存這棟房子原有的裝飾。

sentences.en: The nature reserve was created to ______ the region's rare wildlife.
sentences.zh: 這座自然保護區的成立是為了保護這個地區稀有的野生動物。

words.defn_en: to assume something to be true:

sentences.en: I ______ he will be late to the party.
sentences.zh: 我猜想他派對會遲到。

sentences.en: You shouldn't ______ that everyone shares your opinion.
sentences.zh: 你不應該假定每個人都認同你的看法。

words.defn_en: an assumption taken as true without proof; arrogant behavior:

sentences.en: The court operates on the ______ of innocence until proven guilty.
sentences.zh: 法院是根據無罪推定的原則運作的,直到證明有罪為止。

sentences.en: His ______ in speaking for the entire group offended several members.
sentences.zh: 他擅自代表整個團體發言的放肆行為冒犯了好幾位成員。

words.defn_en: the quality of being overly bold or arrogant:

sentences.en: His ______ in criticizing the CEO's decision shocked the entire room.
sentences.zh: 他批評執行長決定時的放肆態度震驚了整個會場。

sentences.en: She apologized for the ______ of assuming she'd already been invited.
sentences.zh: 她為擅自假設自己已被邀請的放肆行為道了歉。

words.defn_en: an appearance or action intended to deceive:

sentences.en: He entered the office under the ______ of delivering a package.
sentences.zh: 他以送包裹為藉口進入了這間辦公室。

sentences.en: She dropped all ______ of politeness once the meeting ended.
sentences.zh: 會議一結束,她便放下了所有禮貌的偽裝。

words.defn_en: to prove more powerful or superior; to win or succeed after a struggle:

sentences.en: After a long legal battle, justice finally ______.
sentences.zh: 經過一場漫長的法律訴訟,正義終於獲得伸張。

sentences.en: Justice will always ______.
sentences.zh: 正義終將獲勝。

words.defn_en: to stop something from happening:

sentences.en: Vaccination can ______ the spread of many infectious diseases.
sentences.zh: 接種疫苗能預防許多傳染病的擴散。

sentences.en: A last-minute call helped ______ the deal from falling apart.
sentences.zh: 一通最後一刻的電話幫助阻止了這筆交易的破裂。

words.defn_en: able to be avoided:

sentences.en: Many diseases are ______ with vaccines.
sentences.zh: 許多疾病是可以透過疫苗預防的。

sentences.en: The report concluded that most of the accidents were entirely ______.
sentences.zh: 這份報告的結論是,大多數的意外其實都是可以預防的。
